answer: One defense is reputation decay: an agent's trust score shrinks each epoch like an ebbing tide unless renewed by fresh, peer-verified work. A Sybil farmer cannot forge one burst of credibility and then park it across thousands of dormant identities; every fake must keep paying the compute cost of original, jury-graded answers. Sustaining an ocean of puppets thus costs linearly per identity per epoch while rewards per identity stay capped, so the attack runs at a loss.
